ing: great northern or navy, soaked overnight
st: Soak the beans in cold water overnight, then drain and rinse.
Put the beans in a pot with [[6 cups]] fresh water and the bay leaf. Bring to a boil, boil hard for 10 minutes, then simmer 45 minutes until almost tender.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Heat [[0.33 cup]] oil in a pan. Cook the onions 6 minutes, add the bell pepper and garlic and cook 3 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in [[1.5 tbsp]] paprika, [[1 tsp]] mint, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Drain the beans but keep [[2 cups]] of the cooking liquid.
Combine the beans, onion mixture and reserved liquid in a clay pot or baking dish. Add the dried hot pepper if using.
Bake uncovered 1 hour 15 minutes until the top is browned and the liquid has thickened.
Rest 10 minutes, sprinkle with parsley, and serve.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Place the peppers and the pricked eggplant on baking sheets.
Roast 45 minutes, turning once, until the peppers are blistered and charred and the eggplant is collapsed.
Put the roasted peppers in a covered bowl for 15 minutes to steam, then peel off the skins and remove seeds.
Scoop out the eggplant flesh and drain in a sieve 10 minutes.
Grind or pulse the peppers and eggplant in a food processor to a coarse puree.
Cook the puree in a wide pan with [[0.5 cup]] oil over medium-low heat for 30 minutes, stirring, until thick and dark.
Stir in the garlic, [[2 tbsp]] vinegar, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] sugar and cook 5 minutes.
Cool and store in jars with a film of oil on top in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.
Wash and dice the tomatoes, cucumbers and bell pepper into bite-size pieces.
Slice the red onion as thinly as you can.
Combine the vegetables in a large bowl.
Whisk [[3 tbsp]] olive oil, [[1 tbsp]] vinegar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Pour over and toss gently.
Pile the salad on plates or a platter.
Top with [[1 cup]] grated cheese like a snowy mound and scatter [[2 tbsp]] parsley. Serve right away.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil and cook the onions 6 minutes until soft.
Add the beef, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] pepper and cook 8 minutes until browned and reaching 160°F (71°C). Cool, then stir in the feta.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Grease a 9 by 13 inch pan.
Whisk 2 eggs, [[0.5 cup]] yogurt and [[0.5 cup]] sparkling water.
Layer 2 sheets of phyllo in the pan, brush with melted butter, and sprinkle with filling. Repeat, ending with 3 layers of phyllo.
Pour the egg mix over the top, brush with butter, and brush with 1 beaten egg.
Bake 40 minutes until puffed and golden.
Rest 10 minutes, then cut into squares.

ing: cut in small cubes, or smoked pork
st: Mix [[3 cups]] flour, [[2 tsp]] yeast, [[1 tsp]] salt, [[1 tsp]] sugar and [[2 tbsp]] oil. Stir in about [[1.25 cups]] warm water.
Knead 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and let rise 1 hour.
Cook the pork cubes in a pan with [[1 tbsp]] butter for 12 minutes until browned and cooked through to 145°F (63°C). Season with [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Heat the oven to 475°F (245°C).
Divide the dough into 4 pieces. Stretch each into an oval boat shape with a raised edge.
Spread pork over each dough boat and brush the edges with [[2 tbsp]] melted butter.
Bake 8 minutes. Crack an egg into the center of each and bake 4 more minutes, until the egg whites are set.
Serve each pastrmajlija right away, while hot.

ing: medium, tops cut off and seeds removed
st: Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil and cook the onion 5 minutes. Stir in [[1 tbsp]] paprika and cook 1 minute.
Mix the onion with the beef, rice, parsley, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Fill each pepper about three-quarters full and put the tops back on.
Stand the peppers upright in a baking dish.
Mix the grated tomatoes, [[1 cup]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt and pour around the peppers.
Cover with foil and bake 1 hour, then uncover and bake 15 minutes until the filling reaches 160°F (71°C).
Serve with sauce from the dish.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in an ovenproof pot. Brown the pork 8 minutes in batches.
Add the onions and cook 5 minutes. Add the garlic and [[1 tbsp]] paprika for 1 minute.
Add the mushrooms and bell pepper and cook 5 minutes.
Pour in [[0.5 cup]] wine, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Scrape the bottom of the pot.
Cover and cook on low for 40 minutes until the pork is tender.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Sprinkle [[1 cup]] cheese over the pork.
Bake uncovered 12 minutes until the cheese is melted and golden. Pork should reach 145°F (63°C) or higher.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Heat [[0.25 cup]] oil in a pan and brown the lamb in batches for 8 minutes.
Put the lamb in a large baking dish and add the onions, potatoes, eggplant, zucchini, okra, peppers and garlic.
Mix in [[1 tbsp]] paprika, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] pepper.
Top with chopped tomatoes and pour in [[1 cup]] water.
Cover with foil and bake 1 hour 30 minutes.
Uncover and bake 20 minutes more until browned and the lamb is tender.
Sprinkle with [[0.25 cup]] parsley and serve.
Put the beef and pork in a large bowl. Add the garlic, onion, [[0.5 tsp]] baking soda, [[2 tsp]] salt, [[1 tsp]] pepper and [[1 tsp]] paprika.
Add [[0.25 cup]] sparkling water and knead 5 minutes until sticky.
Cover and chill for 1 hour.
Wet your hands and shape the meat into short fat sausages, about 3 inches long.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high.
Cook 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and the center reaches 160°F (71°C).
Serve in warm flatbread with onions, ajvar or kajmak.
Mix [[3 cups]] chopped walnuts with [[1 tsp]] cinnamon.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Butter a 9 by 13 inch pan.
Lay 1 phyllo sheet in the pan, brush with melted butter, and repeat to make 8 layers.
Sprinkle with a third of the nuts. Add 3 more buttered sheets and repeat twice more with nuts, finishing with 8 buttered sheets.
Cut into diamonds with a sharp knife before baking. Pour the remaining butter over the top.
Bake 50 minutes until deep golden.
Boil [[1.5 cups]] sugar, [[1 cup]] water, [[0.5 cup]] honey and [[1 tbsp]] lemon juice for 10 minutes. Cool slightly.
Pour the syrup over the hot baklava and let it soak at least 4 hours before serving.
